title: WHY LATIN LETTERS?
sub: Vietnamese is written in a Latin-based alphabet called quốc ngữ. How did that happen?
say: Vietnamese is written in a Latin-based alphabet called kwok ngoo. How did that happen?

title: BEFORE
sub: For centuries, Vietnamese elites wrote in Literary Chinese. They also used chữ Nôm, Chinese-based characters adapted to write Vietnamese.
say: For centuries, Vietnamese elites wrote in Literary Chinese. They also used chuh Nome, Chinese-based characters adapted to write Vietnamese.

title: 1620s
sub: In the early 1600s, Jesuit missionaries began writing Vietnamese in Latin letters, to learn the language and to preach. Francisco de Pina, a Portuguese Jesuit, was one of the pioneers.
say: In the early sixteen hundreds, Jesuit missionaries began writing Vietnamese in Latin letters, to learn the language and to preach. Fran-sis-ko deh Pee-nah, a Portuguese Jesuit, was one of the pioneers.

sub: In 1651, the French Jesuit Alexandre de Rhodes published a Vietnamese–Portuguese–Latin dictionary in Rome. He is often called the inventor, but he built on the work of others.
say: In sixteen fifty-one, the French Jesuit Alex-ahndr deh Rode published a Vietnamese–Portuguese–Latin dictionary in Rome. He is often called the inventor, but he built on the work of others.

title: 200 YEARS
sub: For about two centuries, its use stayed limited.
say: For about two centuries, its use stayed limited.

title: COLONIAL ERA
sub: Under French rule, the colonial state promoted quốc ngữ. The old Confucian examination system ended in 1919.
say: Under French rule, the colonial state promoted kwok ngoo. The old Confucian examination system ended in nineteen nineteen.

title: REFORMERS
sub: Vietnamese reformers also embraced it. Founded in Hanoi in 1907, the Tonkin Free School taught quốc ngữ alongside Chinese and French.
say: Vietnamese reformers also embraced it. Founded in Hanoi in nineteen oh seven, the Tonkin Free School taught kwok ngoo alongside Chinese and French.

sub: After 1945, the new Vietnamese government ran mass literacy campaigns in quốc ngữ. Today it is simply how Vietnamese is written.
say: After nineteen forty-five, the new Vietnamese government ran mass literacy campaigns in kwok ngoo. Today it is simply how Vietnamese is written.

title: TWO VIEWS
sub: Some scholars argue that colonial language policy weakened access to older Hán–Nôm literature. Others stress how Vietnamese reformers and the state later used quốc ngữ to spread literacy.
say: Some scholars argue that colonial language policy weakened access to older Hahn Nome literature. Others stress how Vietnamese reformers and the state later used kwok ngoo to spread literacy.

title: RICE & EMPIRES
sub: A script begun by missionaries later became Vietnam's national writing system. Follow for more.
